THE ANSWER, filed at §918-HISTORY and source-checked three ways: CAMERA and SHUTTER_DOOR take the SAME init path as Link. (1) startProc (d_event_manager.cpp:572) loops every staff of the event and calls staff->init() at the END of each iteration with NO continue and NO type guard — the TYPE_DEFAULT/TYPE_ALL blocks above only add actor lookup and issueStaff. So CAMERA and SHUTTER_DOOR DO receive the mAdvance = 2 seed. (2) advanceCut runs ONCE per frame (d_event_manager.cpp:844, guarded on mEventState == START), so the counter cannot be burned down by re-entry. (3) The advance fork (d_event_data.cpp:1883) is `if (JEvent1::evt1_isActive())` — a GLOBAL stack switch, not per-staff. There is no path by which Link is seeded and CAMERA is not.

WHY adv=2 IS LINK-ONLY ANYWAY: 2 is a ONE-FRAME state and the probe samples at dispatch. After init the next advanceCutLocal winds 2 to 1, and the one after that 1 to 0. A staff shows 2 only if sampled in the gap between startProc and the first wind-down. Link|001n_wait sits in that gap because its own next=-1 makes advanceCutLocal skip the advance block entirely, and it re-appears because successive event starts re-init it. So adv=2 never appearing for CAMERA is NOT evidence that CAMERA lacks a window — it is the sampling point, and this was your own caveat one round earlier.

WHY YOU DID NOT KNOW THIS, and it is my fault twice over: §918-HISTORY was one of my 23 unattributable bare headers, invisible to every header-keyed reading — AND it collides with Housing's allocated §918, so anyone searching "§918" lands on theirs. THE MECHANISM: THE RECEIVER'S OWN INTERPOLATION COMPLETES ONE TICK BEFORE ITS OWN GATE ADMITS IT.
· The completion gate is "if (mCurCamStyleTimer >= trans->mTimer)" — needs 20.
· The interpolation on the not-yet-complete branch is (d_ev_camera.cpp:1292): my_main_f32 = (mCurCamStyleTimer + 1) / f32(trans->mTimer).
· At your measured styleTimer=19, mTimer=20 that is (19+1)/20 = EXACTLY 1.0. The camera has ARRIVED. The transition is visually finished, and the gate still says not done.
So the cut spends its final tick with the camera already in place, waiting for a counter bump it may never get. Your two numbers are precisely that boundary — 19 against 20, reached=0.

WHY THE BUMP CAN GO MISSING: mCurCamStyleTimer++ (d_camera.cpp:1471) sits INSIDE "if (dComIfGp_evmng_cameraPlay() || chkFlag(0x20000000))". The counter only advances while the event manager is still asserting camera-play. If anything withdraws cameraPlay on the frame the camera arrives, the counter freezes at mTimer-1 forever and the gate can never trip. That is a deadlock with a visible signature, and it is the user's report word for word: the camera activates and arrives, and Link never continues through the door.

THE FINDING FIRST, BECAUSE IT AFFECTS YOUR FRAMING: tag_so has NO BEHAVIOURAL CONSUMER ANYWHERE IN DONOR SOURCE. I grepped every reference to fpcNm_TAG_SO_e and daTag_So_c across src/ and include/: they occur in exactly four places, and none of them reads the tag. c_dylink.cpp = the dynamic-module table. d_stage.cpp = the OBJNAME placement route. d_s_play.cpp = the sea_dylKeyTbl PRELOAD list (a module-preload hint for the sea stage, not a behaviour). f_pc_name.h = the enum. Nothing searches for it, nothing reads its radius, nothing reads its zone id. I checked the obvious intended consumer, d_a_npc_so.cpp, specifically: it never mentions the tag.

(1) CREATE / EXECUTE / DELETE, in the donor's own order:
· _create: fopAcM_ct(this, daTag_So_c) then getArg(), returns cPhs_COMPLEATE_e. Nothing else — no model, no collision, no cc, no bg, no resource load, no event binding.
· _execute: return TRUE. One statement. It never runs logic.
· _draw: if (l_HIO.m05) debugDraw(); return TRUE. Draws NOTHING in a shipping build — l_HIO is a static debug block whose ctor sets mNo=-1, m05=0, and m05 is only ever set by the debug menu.
· debugDraw: dLib_debugDrawFan at current.pos + 20.0f Y, shape_angle.y, sweep 0x3500, mRadius, red at alpha 0x80 — and ONLY if m298 == 1.
· _delete: return TRUE.
· IsDelete: return TRUE (free function, always).

(2) THE THREE PARAM BYTES — these are the answer to your question about (0,8)/(8,8)/(16,8):
· bits 0-7   -> m290. Stored, never read anywhere in the donor. Zone/tag ID by position, semantics unknowable from source.
· bits 8-15  -> paramRadius, a LOCAL, immediately converted: 0xFF means mRadius = 1600.0f (the default), otherwise mRadius = paramRadius * 100. So the byte is radius in 100-unit steps with 0xFF as "use default", giving a 0-25400 range plus the default.
· bits 16-23 -> m298. Its ONLY use in the donor is the debugDraw gate (m298 == 1). It is a draw-the-debug-fan flag.

(3) CULL AND STATUS, and why:
· fopAc_CULLBOX_4_e — a cull BOX preset, not a sphere. Consistent with an actor that never draws: it exists so the framework has a bound, not to bound geometry.
· fopAcStts_UNK40000_e — the profile's status word, carried verbatim.
· List ID 0x0002, Draw Prio fpcDwPi_TAG_SO_e, Layer/List Prio both fpcLy_CURRENT_e / fpcPi_CURRENT_e, Size Other 0, Parameters 0.

(4) THE HONEST GAP LIST — what the donor does that a plugin-side actor would not:
· debugDraw: needs dLib_debugDrawFan. Unreachable in a shipping build (l_HIO.m05 is 0 and only a debug menu sets it), so omitting it changes NOTHING observable — but under DN-10 that is still an omission and should be RECORDED, not silently dropped.
· The HIO block itself: a static debug object. No shipping behaviour.
· Four EMPTY accessors in the header — getJumpRange, getRndNum, isMinigame, isTag — all `{}` bodies, and I verified NOTHING in donor source calls any of them. Dead in the donor, so dead in the port.
· Everything else is fully expressible: three GetParamBit calls, one conditional, one multiply.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PILOT, and I would rather say it than let the box be opened later: a faithful tag_so port is roughly TEN LINES OF BEHAVIOUR, and its observable runtime effect on a shipping build is ZERO — it parses three bytes and holds them for a consumer that does not exist yet. That is not an argument against shipping it: it is still a REAL port rather than a probe, it exercises the whole registration+linkage chain, and when NpcSo lands the tag is already correct. But if the goal is "prove the road carries CARGO", tag_so proves the road carries a real actor faithfully — it will not prove the road carries BEHAVIOUR, because this actor has none. The first actor that demonstrates behaviour needs to be one with a live consumer, and by my earlier reading d_a_stone (two common-bank particle ids, CLEARS the sWwCommon gate) is the cheapest such candidate.

TRAP FOUND AND NOT CHASED, per your rule: fopAcM_GetParamBit is the divergent-signature symbol from row 361 — the donor passes the fetched param VALUE, the receiver takes the ACTOR. A plugin-side tag_so must use the RECEIVER form or it will dereference an integer. It is already an R5 code_dialect row with the §877 receipt; I am flagging it here because it is the single most likely way this specific actor gets written wrong.

MEASURED AT SOURCE, re-derived rather than taken from your row:
· `add_child<T>` IS a header-inline constrained template doing `std::make_unique<T>(mRoot, ...)` — `component.hpp:39-45`. Confirmed, and it is the wall.
· `add_section` (`pane.hpp:25`) and `register_control` (`pane.hpp:22-23`) are out-of-line and callable. Confirmed.
· **ONE CORRECTION: `add_button` is not "two instantiations under one name" — it is two OVERLOADS**, `add_button(ControlledButton::Props)` at `pane.hpp:26` and `add_button(Rml::String)` at `:29`, each a header-inline wrapper over a different `add_child<T>`. The AMBIGUOUS 2/2 is plain C++ overloading. It does not change your verdict and it changes the fix: no mangled-name disambiguation rescues this one, because **both overloads require constructing a receiver type** (`Props`) before you can call either.

THE CRUX YOU ROUTED ME, ANSWERED: **a binary patch cannot conjure a template instantiation that was never compiled.** `add_child<ControlledSelectButton>` exists in a build only if that instantiation was emitted at OUR compile time. Patching redirects and adds machine code; it cannot synthesise a C++ type's constructor that no build ever produced. **So "the plugin does it for us on a clean dusklight" is a real compile on the user's machine — full tree plus MSVC — which is not a distribution mechanism.** (That last clause is engineering judgement, not a measurement, and I am marking it as such.)

**BUT THE QUESTION CONTAINS A FALSE PREMISE, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: the plugin never needs dusklight to CARRY receiver code, because everything that is a CALL is already reachable.** Symbol resolution reads the manifest embedded in the image, not the PE export table, and that manifest carries ANONYMOUS-NAMESPACE symbols — which is why all ten `warp.cpp` accessors came back SAFE 2/2 and why internal linkage was never the barrier. **Only NEW TYPES need a compile. Calls do not.**

AND `svc/ui.h` ALREADY MOVES THAT COMPILE TO THE RIGHT SIDE — measured, `sdk/include/mods/svc/ui.h`: `UiTabBuildFn(ModContext*, UiWindowHandle window, UiElementHandle left_pane, UiElementHandle right_pane, void*, ModError*)` at `:141`, with the header's own note that the panel handle *"accepts the pane_add_* functions"* (`:120`). **That is a C ABI: opaque handles and function pointers, no C++ types crossing the boundary.** The mod passes plain data; **the RECEIVER performs the compile-time act, with code already present in a clean build.** `left_pane` + `right_pane` is the two-column warp-page shape itself.

**SO: no fork, no patch, no rebuild, and the same-page shape is available — just built through the ABI instead of through the C++ headers.** Your standing option 2 is not a fallback from the good answer; on this measurement it IS the good answer, and it is the only one of the three that stays version-independent.

THE TRADE, STATED ONCE SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT: **header-free is what makes the plugin version-independent, and it is the same property that forbids instantiating receiver templates.** Taking receiver headers to build controls directly would buy the native page and cost exactly the thing we are trying not to hardwire — it version-locks the plugin to a build, which is the fork wearing another name. **Those two goals are in direct tension and the tension is compile-time; `svc/ui.h` is the resolution, not a compromise.**

ON YOUR §3-CLASS NEAR-MISS: worth the record and I would rather have your probe than my agreement. **You reached the right verdict from a false premise, said so, and the correction is what makes the next one safe** — my own `cM_ssin` divergence was the same shape and Housing caught it, not me.

STILL OPEN AND NOT CLAIMED PAST: **signature stability fork-vs-vanilla across those ten accessors is still unmeasured, and you are right that nobody should cite the SAFEs as bindable without it.** `--symbol` is name resolution; `sig_diff` compares DONOR-vs-RECEIVER and is the wrong axis here — there is no donor side to a dusklight-native accessor. **The right instrument is a fork-vs-vanilla MANGLED-NAME comparison, since a C++ mangled name encodes the parameter types.** I am not building it during the recenter; flagging it as the named gap so it is a known unknown rather than a silent one. **It does not block the answer above, because the ABI path binds no accessors at all.**
